source.title: ResMLP: Feedforward Networks for Image Classification With Data-Efficient Training
source.authors: Hugo Touvron; P. Bojanowski; Mathilde Caron; M. Cord; Alaaeldin El-Nouby; E. Grave; Gautier Izacard; A. Joulin; Gabriel Synnaeve; Jakob Verbeek; Hervé Jégou

record.tranche_reason: Compares a fully connected, patch-based image classifier with convolutional architectures and reports held-out accuracy, but does not reproduce the specified MNIST/CIFAR comparisons or isolate local connectivity as the cause.
record.gate_note: The paper reports architecture comparisons and ablations on ImageNet. It does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, large-batch generalization, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Table 1 includes published reference architectures; those reported comparisons are recorded as comparators, not treated as new training runs.
record.test_reason: The study extends the convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison to patch-based residual MLPs on ImageNet, including its own convolutional replacement experiments. Its training-recipe progression also contains a LAMB-to-SGD comparison, although this is not an isolated comparison against the default recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but should attribute the absence of spatial priors to the authors' characterization. They conclude that a simple patch-based residual MLP achieves unexpectedly strong ImageNet performance with modern training, while its accuracy/compute trade-off remains worse than convolutional and transformer references. Learned interactions include convolution-like local patterns and sparse long-range connections. Similar or slightly greater validation overfitting is a subsidiary finding.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a residual MLP with patch interaction, modern ImageNet training and accuracy comparisons; it does not reproduce the specified original studies' interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: ImageNet validation versus ImageNet-V2 comparison; architecture and patch-communication choice; training recipe and optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing patch communication reduces validation accuracy from 76.6% to 56.5%; replacing the linear communication with an MLP gives 77.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-patch communication substantially improves this patch-based classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: ResMLP has similar or slightly greater relative validation-to-V2 overfitting than comparison architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture can affect apparent overfitting to validation-based hyperparameter selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-supervised, transferred, and distilled ResMLPs achieve competitive image-classification results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining and distillation can make patch-based MLP features competitive; these settings do not establish V3's comparison between networks trained from scratch.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: Architecture comparisons include published reference results rather than a matched retraining experiment. The principal generalization comparison uses validation and ImageNet-V2 rather than a standard held-out split from the same distribution; uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and fixed-random-label training or random-label held-out evaluation.
No width sweep locating zero training error and testing further widening.

No reproduction of the original small-image experiments, causal attribution of much of the advantage to locality, or convolutional-weight initialization experiment. Learned sparse local patterns are visualized, but their effect on the architectural accuracy difference is not isolated.
No optimizer tuning study, training-performance comparison, broad benchmark comparison, optimizer switching, or controlled decoupled-weight-decay experiment.
No isolated batch-size comparison under a common epoch budget. The batch-size entry in Table D.1 follows multiple other recipe changes.
No dropout intervention; stochastic depth is a different intervention.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps.
No identification or removal of memorized examples.

missing.what: Record convolution-replacement accuracy on ImageNet-real and V2: linear baseline 83.3/64.4; full convolution 84.4/65.7; depth-wise 83.4/64.6; depth-separable 84.0/65.5. These qualify the validation-only architectural ordering.
missing.locator: Table 3, Baseline models and Patch communication

missing.what: Record the 73.2% recipe entry immediately preceding the SGD step, with the accumulated augmentation-removal conditions, so the optimizer comparison is not attributed to the 76.6% default.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used. ResMLP is a structured patch-based MLP with shared operations, rather than an unrestricted dense pixel-level network. Table D.1 should be interpreted as a recipe progression, not independent changes against the default. No uncertainty estimates establish whether the small convolution-replacement differences are reliable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipes.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks across the interpolation threshold.
No matched-size MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, or SVHN comparison; no sparse-local-connection learning or convolutional initialization experiment.
Only one ImageNet training-recipe ablation compares the default optimizer with SGD; no broad benchmark or optimizer tuning comparison.
No controlled comparison of batch sizes and held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout ablation or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No sharpness or norm/margin measure is compared with training–test gaps.
No identification and removal of memorized examples.

rows.subject: ResMLP-S12
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet training recipe ablation replacing the default optimizer with SGD.
rows.note: The paper's table labels the ablation 'SGD optimizer'; comparison is to the DeiT-style recipe.
rows.check: The default optimizer is LAMB. Table D.1 presents a progression back toward the ResNet recipe: the preceding entry is 73.2% after augmentation removals, followed by 72.1% with SGD. The 76.6% default is not an isolated optimizer baseline; optimizer-specific tuning is unspecified.
